questions.q: In the worked example, when is the gradient-boosted model actually fit?
options: Once, on the full dataset, before any validation happens
Fresh inside each fold of the purged walk-forward validation loop, never once on the full dataset first
Only after seeing the out-of-sample results
It is never fit -- only feature importances are computed
questions.explain: The model is deliberately fit fresh inside each validation fold rather than once on the whole dataset beforehand, avoiding the bolted-on-after-the-fact validation mistake warned about in the kickoff lesson.

questions.q: Why does the validation loop include a purge gap and an embargo around each test fold?
options: To make the code run faster
Because the forward-looking label (e.g., a 5-day-forward return) would otherwise let information leak across the train/test boundary
To artificially inflate the Sharpe ratio
Purge and embargo are not actually used in the example
questions.explain: Because the label looks several days into the future, a purge gap before the test fold and an embargo after it prevent the overlapping label window from leaking information between training and test data.

questions.q: What is computed to measure out-of-sample predictive power in the worked example?
options: Training accuracy only
The Information Coefficient (rank correlation between predictions and actual outcomes) computed per validation fold
The number of features in the dataset
The raw count of buy signals generated
questions.explain: The example uses scipy's spearmanr to compute the Information Coefficient between predictions and actual outcomes within each held-out fold.

questions.q: Why does the lesson emphasize looking at the fold-by-fold IC series rather than just the mean IC?
options: The mean IC is always mathematically incorrect
A healthy-looking mean IC can hide a signal that performed well in only a couple of folds and collapsed in the rest
Fold-by-fold results are required by law for quant research
The mean cannot be computed from a pandas Series
questions.explain: This ties back to Lesson 21's stability lesson: an average metric can mask regime-dependent instability that only shows up when you inspect results fold by fold.

questions.q: If the fold-by-fold IC swings between positive and negative values with a wide standard deviation, what is the honest conclusion according to the lesson?
options: The model should be deployed immediately with high confidence
The results should be hidden from the capstone write-up
This particular feature set and label show weak or no robust signal -- which is a legitimate, useful finding, not a failure
The purge window should be removed to improve results
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames an unstable, inconsistent IC series as an honest and legitimate capstone finding -- weak or absent robust signal -- rather than something to suppress or spin as a success.
